The evidence chunks are essentially identical across all genes (all rated critic_relevance=2/5, all "mention=no"), meaning none of the provided literature directly links any specific gene to the patient's phenotype. I must rely on prior biological knowledge.

The patient's phenotype: proximal+distal limb weakness, highly elevated CK, increased endomysial connective tissue, Gowers sign, joint contractures, respiratory insufficiency, areflexia — this is a muscular dystrophy/congenital myopathy picture. POMK (protein-O-mannose kinase) causes a congenital muscular dystrophy with elevated CK, muscle weakness, contractures, and respiratory involvement. None of the other candidates (LALBA=milk protein, FOXJ1=cilia, ACOT2=acyl-CoA thioesterase, OR13C9=olfactory receptor, MSANTD3=unknown, ALS2=motor neuron disease, ZNF610=zinc finger, FOXA2=transcription factor, ATP8A2=phospholipid flippase, HECW2=ubiquitin ligase, NKX2-6=transcription factor, MAGOH=splicing, PPP1CC=phosphatase, MMP16=matrix metalloproteinase) have established links to this specific muscular dystrophy phenotype profile as strongly as POMK.
